author: VanZandtVS
body:
> I do NOT want to have to go outside for the sole purpose of playing this game.

Good news:  90% of this game can be accessed from your couch.  That may change here shortly with the new Towers of Olympia content, but as of right this instant you can do most everything from your house.

About the only thing I can think of you can't really do from home is Amity hunts, although I've had the Memory structures spawn close enough by to be tagged from the couch it's only been rarely.  With Mnemonics being a precious (relatively limited) resource you wouldn't want to waste them if you're not going to want to finish them because you might have to take a walk.

Now, with the above said, your farming / questing will be more *efficient* if you're willing / capable of moving around, and I mean *ALOT* more efficient in some cases (I'm looking at you Storyline kill quests).  For example, I've got 7 dungeons within view distance of my home base, and if I wanted I could use my wayvessel to get to a friend's base where I can access up to 8 or so more, so without moving I can access 15 dungeons an hour.   If I'm mobile (riding with the wife to get groceries for instance), that number is limited only by a factor of how many dungeons you can find and how fast you can clear them.

Likewise on the questing side of things, if you're looking for a particular quest monster you'll definitely find what you're looking for faster usually if you're moving around, though you will eventually get them to spawn at your base by murdering enough of the local wildlife and monsters.

author: So_Numb13
body:
I'd say you can do 90% from home, might take a bit longer is all. The only things you'll miss are the "exploration" and "control" of areas, since you need to be in those areas to either battle the monster (explore, can only do it once per area) or battle other players for control (you can lose the territory again). But these two things just add to the game (better rewards), I don't think you'll be blocked if you never do them. (Might be an early quest, can't remember).

I usually play from home, and do the exploration and control stuff either on public transport or as a passenger in a car.

There's also a thing called "memory hunt" where stations/mini-games spawn around you and you have to hit 5 to get special items. Sometimes they spawn close enough you can hit them from where you are, sometimes they're out of range and you need to walk there. But I usually don't bother when that's the case. 

The game also spawns buildings when someone starts to play in a new area. I didn't have a dungeon near me at first, then it popped out after a couple months. 

And finally you can join a party and move to their areas through a portal. 

So yeah totally playable from home unless you're a completionist or very impatient.


Oh almost forgot: there's a new version of the game that's not gps related, plays as old fashioned rpg. It's called Hero of Aethric, haven't played myself though.

author: Evoker42
body:
The game is fun even when at home. You will have a building that can have a dungeon added on in an upgrade later as well. Monsters will spawn around you just fine and never run out. The issues can come from the following:

1. Bosses.
2. Control/Exploration. (These are the 'circles' you'll see for land. There's the control aspect which is what you/others 'control' and 'exploration' is simply a once-only fight with an NPC. Do you need to do this? Not really. The 'bonus in items' isn't high. It's just 'neat' if you want to control your own area. I like taking over places I visit. Especially further away or when on a trip.)
3. Dungeons. (Is it needed? Potentially. For story/side quests. Also good for gear/orns/gold, but it isn't a requirement for either.)
4. Amenity. (I've not really had to 'travel' too far for these and have done a few from my own home.)

A lot you can do from the couch. You can join a kingdom and do raids and the like without ever needing to use the 'GPS' aspect of the game.

As someone said, Hero of Aethric if you want the same game without any of the GPS. I, however, personally like the GPS. If I'm out somewhere and want to tag a place in the 'real world' as mine? I could potentially do that! It's neat to me; but it isn't required.

Eventually you'll get to a point in the game (this is faster or slower depending on how 'active' you are) where you can fight the 'top dogs' in your area to boot them out. The game, however, is just that: a game. You don't need to no life it. You don't need to travel the world to enjoy it. A lot you can do from the house; but it's nice to have that 'option' when you're on a 10 minutes trip to... several hours. It's also nice to have it if you're in a new location and just want to tag spots, explore, or see what world bosses might be around!

Note: If you're in the middle of nowhere, it can be nice to go for a walk and literally get new locations to pop up because no one else that plays has ever been back there. Got areas like that all over here once you get off the beaten trails/roads.
